meta.title: Epic kingdoms atlas
methodology: Places are pinned at approximate modern locations; identifications of ancient janapadas are scholarly proposals, not certainties.
Places outside today's India (Gandhara, Kekaya, Madra, Kamboja, Bahlika, Lanka) are drawn as hollow markers on the nearest edge of the map frame with a note.
Alliances follow the epic's war narrative and are simplified; where participation is unclear a place is marked neutral / unclear.

Sanskrit verses are shown only when copied verbatim from a source page listed in 'verified_from'. Where no verse about the exact place could be checked, a verified general verse of the epic is shown and labelled as such. Verse numbering follows that page's edition and may differ from the BORI critical edition.
Routes join the places in the order the epic narrates them; straight segments are a schematic, not the paths the heroes walked.
Descriptions and translations are original summaries, not quotations of any published translation.

mahabharata.title: Kingdoms of the Mahabharata
mahabharata.edition_note: Place identifications and coordinates are approximate and reflect commonly proposed historical-geographic associations, not certain archaeological boundaries. Roles summarize the Sanskrit epic tradition; political alignments are simplified where factions or participation are uncertain. Verses are copied verbatim from the Sanskrit page named in each entry's 'verified_from' link (Wikisource Mahabharata, Sanskrit Documents Gita); numbering follows that page and may differ from the BORI critical edition. Entries with no verse about that exact place show a verified general verse of the epic, labelled 'General verse of the epic'.

entries.name: Kuru Kingdom (Hastinapura)
entries.role: Hastinapura is the Kuru capital and the center of the succession dispute. Duryodhana's faction fought the Pandavas, and Yudhishthira later ruled the kingdom.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Sabha Parva; Udyoga Parva; Bhishma Parva; others
entries.description: The Kuru court's inheritance conflict drives the epic toward the great war. Hastinapura remains the principal seat of Kuru power before and after the conflict.

shloka.sa:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
shloka.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?
shloka.edition: Sanskrit Documents online text (edition not specified)
shloka.note: The source numbers this verse १-१; it names the Kuru field, rather than Hastinapura itself.

entries.allegiance_role: Hastinapura is the Kuru capital and the center of the succession dispute. Duryodhana's faction fought the Pandavas, and Yudhishthira later ruled the kingdom.

entries.name: Kurukshetra (Dharmakshetra)
entries.ruler: Kuru realm; no separate ruler specified
entries.role: Kurukshetra is the battlefield where the Pandava and Kaurava armies meet. Its description as Dharmakshetra frames the war but does not indicate a political side for the place.
entries.description: The eighteen-day war is fought on the plain of Kurukshetra. The Bhagavad Gita opens with Dhritarashtra asking what happened there as the two armies prepared to fight.

entries.name: Indraprastha
entries.role: The Pandavas establish Indraprastha after receiving a portion of the Kuru realm. It becomes their capital before the dice game and their exile.
entries.description: The Pandavas transform their assigned territory into a prosperous city. Its royal assembly and the game of dice mark a turning point in the story.

shloka.sa: इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस्ते त्रीणि वर्षाणि विंशतिम्। द्वादशाब्दानथैकं च बभूवुर्द्यूतनिर्जिताः॥
shloka.translation: They lived at Indraprastha for three and twenty years; then, beaten at dice, they spent twelve years and one more in exile.

entries.name: Panchala (Kampilya and Ahichchhatra)
entries.role: Panchala is the realm of Drupada and Draupadi's homeland. Drupada, Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi, and other Panchala warriors support the Pandavas in the war.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Virata Parva; Bhishma Parva; Drona Parva
entries.description: The kingdom is closely linked to the Pandavas through Draupadi's marriage and Drupada's alliance. Its forces and commanders play a major part in the conflict.

entries.name: Matsya (Virata Kingdom)
entries.role: The Pandavas spend their incognito year at Virata's court. Virata and his family subsequently join the Pandava alliance in the war.
entries.description: Matsya provides refuge to the exiled Pandavas while they conceal their identities. The kingdom's alliance is reinforced through family ties and shared military action.

entries.name: Dvaraka and Anarta (Yadava realm)
entries.role: Krishna supports the Pandavas as Arjuna's charioteer and counselor, while Satyaki and other Yadavas fight for them. Krishna remains unarmed, and Yadava loyalties are not wholly uniform.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Udyoga Parva; Bhishma Parva; Mausala Parva
entries.description: Dvaraka is the western Yadava city associated with Krishna and his kin. The epic presents its people as a politically complex group rather than a single undivided army.

shloka.sa:

shloka.translation: The Pundras, Bhargas, Kiratas, Sudrishtas and Yamunas; the Shakas, Nishadas, Nishadhas, and likewise the Anartas and Nairritas.

entries.name: Mathura (Shurasena)
entries.ruler: Krishna and the Yadava chiefs; no single war ruler specified
entries.role: Mathura is the ancestral Yadava center associated with Krishna and the slaying of Kamsa. Balarama stays out of the Kurukshetra war, so the region's overall alignment is best treated as mixed or unspecified.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Sabha Parva; Udyoga Parva
entries.description: The Shurasena realm is an important setting in Krishna's family history. Political authority and military loyalties among the Yadavas are distributed among several leaders.

entries.name: Magadha
entries.modern_location: South Bihar, around Rajgir and Patna
entries.role: Jarasandha is a powerful rival whom Krishna, Bhima, and Arjuna defeat before the Rajasuya. His son Sahadeva later joins the Pandava side; the kingdom's war alignment is therefore recorded as Pandava, with the succession change noted.
entries.description: Magadha's strength shapes the political landscape before the great war. The change from Jarasandha to his son allows the Pandavas to form a new alliance with the realm.

entries.description: Kashi is an old kingdom centered on the Ganges and is represented among the allied forces. Its inclusion here follows the Pandava army's warrior list rather than a detailed political history.

entries.description: Anga's association with Karna gives the kingdom a central personal connection to the conflict. Karna's loyalty to Duryodhana determines the alignment shown here.

entries.role: Shalya, king of Madra and maternal uncle of Nakula and Sahadeva, is induced to fight for Duryodhana. He later serves as Karna's charioteer and as a Kaurava commander.

entries.description: Madra is connected to both sides through Shalya's family ties. His military service for the Kauravas, despite his relationship with the Pandavas, is a notable source of tension.

shloka.sa:
गोधा मद्रकलिङ्गाश्छ काशयोऽपरकाशयः ।
जठराः कुकुराश्चैव सदशार्णाश्च भारत ।
shloka.translation: The Godhas, Madras and Kalingas, the Kashis and the Aparakashis; the Jatharas, Kukuras, and the Dasharnas too, O Bharata.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.42 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 6-9-42 as on sa.wikisource.org

entries.allegiance_citation: Mahabharata 6.9.42 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
entries.allegiance_role: Shalya led Madra; Duryodhana secured his support through a hospitality ruse before Shalya could reach the Pandavas.

entries.name: Kekaya
entries.modern_location: Punjab region near the Chenab-Jhelum basin, Pakistan
entries.ruler: Kekaya princes; the brothers' factions differed
entries.role: Several Kekaya brothers fight for the Pandavas, while other members of the family support the Kauravas. This entry uses the Pandava label for the prominent allied contingent and notes the divided allegiance.
entries.description: Kekaya was a northwestern kingdom whose royal family did not act as a single faction. Its divided loyalties caution against treating every warrior from the region as belonging to one side.

shloka.sa:
अटवीशिखराश्चैव मेरुभूताश्च मारिष ।
उपावृत्तानुपावृत्ताः स्वराष्ट्राः केकयास्तथा ।
shloka.translation: The Atavishikharas and the Merubhutas, O sire; the Upavrittas, Anupavrittas, Svarashtras, and likewise the Kekayas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.48 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

entries.allegiance_role: The Kekaya brothers split between the Pandava and Kaurava alliances.

entries.name: Sindhu-Sauvira
entries.role: Jayadratha, ruler of Sindhu and linked with Sauvira, is allied with the Kauravas. He plays a pivotal role in the death of Abhimanyu and is later slain by Arjuna.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Bhishma Parva; Drona Parva
entries.description: The western Indus kingdoms enter the story through Jayadratha's marriage to Duryodhana's sister and his military alliance. His actions during the battle shape one of the war's most consequential episodes.

shloka.sa:
तिलभारा मसीराश्च मधुमन्तः सकुन्दकाः।
काश्मीराः सिन्धुसौवीरा गान्धारा दर्शकास्तथा ।
shloka.translation: The Tilabharas, Masiras, Madhumantas and Sakundakas; the Kashmiras, the Sindhu-Sauviras, the Gandharas and the Darshakas.

entries.allegiance_role: Jayadratha, ruler of Sindhu and linked with Sauvira, is allied with the Kauravas. He plays a pivotal role in the death of Abhimanyu and is later slain by Arjuna.

entries.name: Trigarta
entries.modern_location: Kangra and adjoining Himachal Pradesh, India
entries.role: Susharma and the Trigarta warriors fight for the Kauravas. Their repeated attacks on Arjuna are intended to draw him away from the main battlefield.
entries.description: Trigarta's army is known for its commitment to fighting Arjuna. Its use as a diversionary force becomes especially important during the attempt to capture Yudhishthira.

shloka.sa:
ध्वजिन्युत्सवसंकेतास्त्रिगर्ताः शाल्वसेनयः।
व्यूकाः कोकबकाः प्रोष्ठाः समवेगवशास्तथा ।
shloka.translation: The Dhvajinyutsavasanketas, the Trigartas, the Shalvasenis; the Vyukas, Kokabakas, Proshthas and Samavegavashas.

entries.name: Avanti
entries.role: The Avanti brothers Vinda and Anuvinda fight for the Kauravas. They are among the western and central Indian rulers who join Duryodhana's coalition.
entries.description: Avanti, centered on the Malwa plateau, contributes prominent royal warriors to the conflict. The brothers' deaths are recounted in the battle books.

shloka.sa:
कुन्तयोऽवन्तयश्चैव तथैवापरकुन्तयः ।
गोमन्ता मन्दकाः सण्डा विदर्भा रूपवाहिकाः ।
shloka.translation: The Kuntis and the Avantis, and likewise the Aparakuntis; the Gomantas, Mandakas, Sandas, Vidarbhas and Rupavahikas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.43 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

entries.allegiance_role: The Avanti brothers Vinda and Anuvinda fight for the Kauravas. They are among the western and central Indian rulers who join Duryodhana's coalition.

entries.name: Vidarbha
entries.role: Rukmi offers aid but is refused by both Arjuna and Duryodhana, so his force does not join either camp. Vidarbha's wider participation is not clear enough to assign a firm side.
entries.description: Vidarbha is linked to Rukmini's marriage to Krishna and to Rukmi's later offer of military support. The episode illustrates why the kingdom is best marked neutral for the war.

entries.name: Pandya
entries.role: A Pandya ruler is counted among the southern kings who support the Pandavas in the war. The epic's references do not always make the identity and chronology of the king explicit.
entries.description: The Pandya kingdom extends the epic's political map into the far south. Its allied presence is notable, although the surviving narrative offers less detail than for northern powers.

shloka.sa:
चतुर्थभाङ्महाराज भोज इन्द्रसखो बली।
विद्याबलाद्यो व्यजयत्स पाण्ड्यक्रथकैशिकान्।
shloka.translation: The fourth part-sharer, O great king, is the mighty Bhoja, friend of Indra, who by the power of his learning conquered the Pandyas, Krathas and Kaishikas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 2.14.21 (Sabha Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 2-14-21 as on sa.wikisource.org
shloka.note: Names the Pandyas as conquered by Bhoja (Bhishmaka of Vidarbha).

entries.name: Chola and Dravida regions
entries.modern_location: Tamil Nadu and adjoining southern India
entries.ruler: Southern rulers; individual war alignment uncertain
entries.role: The epic names southern peoples and kingdoms, but a single, consistent Chola alignment is not securely established across references. This combined regional entry is conservatively marked neutral/unspecified.
entries.description: Chola and Dravida labels contribute to the epic's broad picture of a subcontinent-wide conflict. Historical boundaries and precise identification of every listed southern group remain debated.

shloka.sa:
कौकुट्टकास्तथा चोलाः कोङ्कणा मालवा नराः ।
समङ्गाः करकाश्चैव कुकुराङ्गारमारिषाः ।
shloka.translation: The Kaukuttakas, and likewise the Cholas, the Konkanas and the Malava people; the Samangas, Karakas, and the Kukuras, Angaras and Marishas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.60 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 6-9-60 as on sa.wikisource.org

entries.name: Kamboja
entries.modern_location: Hindu Kush region, Afghanistan and adjoining Central Asia
entries.ruler: Kamboja chiefs; Sudakshina is associated with its forces
entries.role: Kamboja horsemen and their leader Sudakshina are associated with the Kaurava army. They are presented as formidable cavalry from the northwestern frontier.
entries.description: Kamboja belongs to the epic's frontier geography beyond the northwestern plains. Its mounted troops form one of the notable regional contingents in the war.

shloka.sa:
उत्तराश्चापरे म्लेच्छाः क्रूरा भरतसत्तम।
यवनाश्चीनकाम्बोजा दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः ।
shloka.translation: Other fierce northern peoples, O best of the Bharatas: the Yavanas, Chinas and Kambojas, harsh Mleccha tribes.

entries.name: Shalva
entries.ruler: Shalva king; identity and war participation uncertain
entries.role: The Shalva name is associated with a western kingdom and the story of King Shalva, but its participation in the Kurukshetra war is not sufficiently clear for a firm alignment. It is therefore marked neutral/unspecified.
entries.description: Shalva appears in episodes involving Krishna and in the epic's wider regional geography. Its precise location and military role vary or remain indistinct in the tradition.

shloka.sa:
तत्रेमे कुरुपाञ्चालाः शाल्वा माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः ।
शूरसेनाः पुलिन्दाश्च बोधा मालास्तथैव च ।
shloka.translation: Here are these: the Kurus and Panchalas, the Shalvas, the Madreyas and Jangalas, the Shurasenas, Pulindas, Bodhas and Malas.

entries.name: Nishada peoples and realm
entries.modern_location: Central Indian forest and river regions; location approximate
entries.ruler: Hiranyadhanus; Ekalavya in the Adi Parva episode
entries.role: The Nishada chief Ekalavya is known from the Drona and archery episode, while Nishada identity covers multiple communities in epic geography. No single war alignment for the realm is established, so it is marked neutral.
entries.description: Nishada is a broad people-and-region designation rather than a clearly bounded state. Its inclusion recalls Ekalavya's story without assuming that his community fought in the great war.

shloka.sa:
पुण्ड्रा भर्गाः किराताश्च सुदृष्टा यामुनास्तथा।
शका निषादा निषधास्तथैवानर्तनैर्ऋताः ।
shloka.translation: The Pundras, Bhargas, Kiratas, Sudrishtas and Yamunas; the Shakas, Nishadas, Nishadhas, and likewise the Anartas and Nairritas.

entries.name: Kuntibhoja
entries.ruler: Kuntibhoja; later a warrior of the same royal line
entries.role: Kuntibhoja is the foster father of Kunti and is named among the Pandava-side warriors in the opening of the Gita. The identification of the battlefield warrior with the earlier king is not certain.
entries.description: The kingdom's best-known connection is its adoption of Kunti, who becomes the mother of the Pandavas. A Kuntibhoja warrior's presence in the Pandava army carries that familial association into the war.

shloka.sa:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ।

entries.role: Kashmira is part of the epic's northern geographic horizon, but the accounts do not provide a sufficiently consistent war alignment for the kingdom. It is marked neutral/unspecified.
entries.description: The Kashmira name appears among the northern peoples and regions associated with the wider epic world. Its inclusion is geographic, not a claim that it played a decisive battlefield role.

entries.name: Manipura (Arjuna and Chitrangada's realm)
entries.modern_location: Northeastern India; identification with modern Manipur is traditional but debated
entries.role: Arjuna marries Chitrangada, daughter of the king of Manipura, and their son is Babhruvahana. The kingdom is not assigned a clear part in the Kurukshetra war, so its side is marked neutral.
entries.description: Manipura is connected to Arjuna's journey and to the later horse sacrifice narrative. The epic's place-name should not be assumed to map exactly onto the borders of the modern state.

shloka.sa: एतत्सर्वं यथावृत्तं कथितं भरतर्षभ। यथा तु स हतो राजा भीमसेनेन तच्छृणु॥
shloka.translation: All this, bull among the Bharatas, has been told just as it happened; now hear how that king was slain by Bhimasena.

entries.allegiance_role: Arjuna marries Chitrangada, daughter of the king of Manipura, and their son is Babhruvahana. The kingdom is not assigned a clear part in the Kurukshetra war, so its side is marked neutral.

entries.name: Bahlika (Vahlika)
entries.role: Bahlika is an elder member of the Kuru family and fights in the Kaurava ranks. He is killed during the battle by Bhima.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Bhishma Parva; Drona Parva
entries.description: The name Bahlika is linked with a northwestern kingdom beyond the core Kuru territory. The Bahlika king's kinship with the Kurus makes his participation on Duryodhana's side especially notable.

shloka.sa:
बाह्लीका वाटधानाश्च आभीराः कालतोयकाः।
अपरान्ताः परान्ताश्च पञ्चालाश्चर्ममण्डलाः ।

entries.name: Saurashtra
entries.ruler: Yadava and regional chiefs; no single war alignment specified
entries.role: Saurashtra overlaps the western Yadava sphere associated with Dvaraka, whose leaders and forces did not all take the same course. It is conservatively marked neutral as a region, while Krishna and Satyaki's Pandava support is recorded under Dvaraka.
entries.parva: Adi Parva; Udyoga Parva; Mausala Parva
entries.description: Saurashtra forms the western coastal setting for several Yadava traditions. The region's multiple rulers make a single alignment too simple to state confidently.

shloka.sa: ततो युयुत्सुमानाय्य प्रव्रजन्धर्मकाम्यया। राज्यं परिददौ सर्वं वैश्यापुत्रे युधिष्ठिरः॥
shloka.translation: Then, calling Yuyutsu and setting out in pursuit of dharma, Yudhishthira handed the whole kingdom over to the son of the Vaishya woman.

entries.name: Yavana and Shaka contingents
entries.role: Yavana and Shaka contingents are named among the peoples associated with the Kaurava host; no separate akshauhini count is assigned to them.
entries.description: The Sanskrit geographical and army catalogues name Yavanas and Shakas among frontier peoples. Their precise political boundaries and unit strengths are not specified here.

route.title: The Pandavas’ route and battles
route.summary: From Hastinapura through exile and Indraprastha to the war at Kurukshetra and the final walk to the Himalaya.

stops.name: Kuru Kingdom (Hastinapura)
stops.note: The Pandavas grow up in the Kuru capital.

shloka.sa:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
shloka.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?
shloka.edition: Sanskrit Documents online text (edition not specified)
shloka.note: The source numbers this verse १-१; it names the Kuru field, rather than Hastinapura itself.

stops.name: Varanavata
stops.note: The house of lac is said to have been set alight here; the brothers escaped through a tunnel.

shloka.sa: ततस्तस्मिन्पुरे लोका नगरे वारणावते। दृष्ट्वा जतुगृहं दग्धमन्वशोचन्त दुःखिताः॥
shloka.translation: Then the people of the city of Varanavata, seeing the house of lac burnt, mourned in sorrow.

stops.name: Ekachakra
stops.note: Hiding as Brahmins, they live here until Bhima kills the demon Baka. The location is uncertain.

shloka.sa: जटाः कृत्वाऽऽत्मनः सर्वे वल्कलाजिनवाससः। कुन्त्या सह महात्मानो बिभ्रतस्तापसं वपुः॥
shloka.translation: They all took on matted locks and clothing of bark and deerskin, and with Kunti the great-souled brothers bore the look of ascetics.

stops.name: Panchala (Kampilya and Ahichchhatra)
stops.note: At Draupadi’s svayamvara in Panchala, Arjuna wins her hand.

shloka.sa:
तत्रेमे कुरुपाञ्चालाः शाल्वा माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः ।
शूरसेनाः पुलिन्दाश्च बोधा मालास्तथैव च ।
shloka.translation: Here are these: the Kurus and Panchalas, the Shalvas, the Madreyas and Jangalas, the Shurasenas, Pulindas, Bodhas and Malas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.39 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 6-9-39 as on sa.wikisource.org

stops.name: Indraprastha
stops.note: Yudhishthira founds a kingdom and performs the Rajasuya.

shloka.sa: इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस्ते त्रीणि वर्षाणि विंशतिम्। द्वादशाब्दानथैकं च बभूवुर्द्यूतनिर्जिताः॥
shloka.translation: They lived at Indraprastha for three and twenty years; then, beaten at dice, they spent twelve years and one more in exile.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

stops.name: Magadha
stops.note: Bhima defeats Jarasandha in a duel lasting many days.

shloka.sa:
वारवास्यायवाहाश्च चक्राश्चक्रातयः शकाः।
विदेहा मगधाः स्वक्षा मलजा विजयास्तथा ।
shloka.translation: The Varavasyas, Ayavahas, Chakras, Chakratayas and Shakas; the Videhas, Magadhas, Svakshas, Malajas and Vijayas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.45 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 6-9-45 as on sa.wikisource.org

stops.name: Matsya (Virata Kingdom)
stops.note: In their year in disguise, Arjuna drives off the Kaurava raid on Virata’s cattle.

shloka.sa:
मत्स्याः कुशल्याः सौशल्याः कुंतयः कांतिकोसलाः ।
चेदिमत्स्यकरूशाश्च भोजाः सिन्धुपुलिन्दकाः ।
shloka.translation: The Matsyas, Kushalyas, Saushalyas, Kuntis and Kanti-Kosalas; the Chedis, Matsyas and Karushas, the Bhojas, and the Sindhu-Pulindas.
shloka.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.40 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)
shloka.edition: 6-9-40 as on sa.wikisource.org

stops.name: Kurukshetra (Dharmakshetra)
stops.note: The eighteen-day war between the Pandavas and Kauravas is fought here.

shloka.sa:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
shloka.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?
shloka.edition: Sanskrit Documents online text (edition not specified)

stops.name: Himalaya and Mount Meru (Mahaprasthana)
stops.note: At the end, the brothers set out for the Himalaya on their final journey.

shloka.sa: तं चाप्यतिक्रमन्तस्ते ददृशुर्वालुकार्णवम्। अवैक्षन्त महाशैलं मेरुं शिखरिणां वरम्॥
shloka.translation: Passing beyond that, they saw an ocean of sand, and they beheld the great mountain Meru, best of peaked ranges.

ramayana.title: Places of the Ramayana
ramayana.edition_note: Original descriptions; modern locations are traditional or scholarly identifications, not certain coordinates. Verses are copied verbatim from the Sanskrit page named in each entry's 'verified_from' link (valmikiramayan.net, Sanskrit Documents); some pages give pada-split text. Numbering follows that page and may differ from the critical edition. Entries with no verse about that exact place show a verified general verse of the epic, labelled 'General verse of the epic'.

entries.name: Ayodhya (Kosala)
entries.role: Capital of Kosala and the home of Rama's royal family; the events surrounding Rama's exile begin here.
entries.kanda: Bala Kanda; Ayodhya Kanda; Uttara Kanda
entries.description: The opening city portrait presents Ayodhya as a prosperous, carefully laid-out capital beside the Sarayu. Its royal household and the succession crisis there set the central exile narrative in motion.

shloka.sa:
अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता |
 मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम् ||
shloka.translation: There was a city named Ayodhya, renowned throughout the world, which Manu, lord of humankind, had himself built.
shloka.edition: valmikiramayan.net UTF-8 presentation, Bāla Kāṇḍa Sarga 5 numbering; recension not specified on the page
shloka.note: The site's verse marker is 1-5-6; numbering is reported in kanda.sarga.shloka format.

entries.allegiance_role: Capital of Kosala and the home of Rama's royal family; the events surrounding Rama's exile begin here.

entries.name: Mithila (Videha)
entries.modern_location: Traditionally associated with Janakpur, Madhesh Province, Nepal
entries.role: Janaka's capital and Sita's home; Rama comes here for the bow contest and marries Sita.
entries.description: Mithila is the setting for Rama and Sita's first meeting and marriage. Janaka's court also frames the test of strength involving Shiva's bow.

shloka.sa: एवम् उक्तः स धर्मात्मा जनकेन महात्मना | प्रत्युवाच मुनिर् वीरम् वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदः || १-६६-४
shloka.translation: When the great-souled Janaka, ruler of Mithila, had spoken thus, the righteous, eloquent sage replied to the king.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Janaka's capital and Sita's home; Rama comes here for the bow contest and marries Sita.

entries.name: Kekaya (Rajagriha)
entries.modern_location: Traditionally placed in the northwestern Punjab region; approximate point near 32.6, 73.7 (present-day Pakistan)
entries.role: Bharata's maternal homeland; Bharata is away there when Rama is exiled and Dasharatha dies.
entries.description: The epic situates Bharata with his maternal relatives in Kekaya during the crisis in Ayodhya. The precise historical location of the kingdom and its Rajagriha is uncertain, so the coordinate is only indicative.

shloka.sa: दत्तपथ्यशना दूताजग्मुः स्वम् स्वम् निवेशनम् | केकयांस्ते गमिष्यन्तो हयानारुह्य सम्मतान् || २-६८-१०
shloka.translation: The messengers, preparing to go to Kekaya, took provisions, mounted their fine horses, and returned to their respective homes.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Bharata's maternal homeland; Bharata is away there when Rama is exiled and Dasharatha dies.

entries.name: Kishkindha
entries.role: Vanara realm where Rama allies with Sugriva and helps him regain the kingdom; it becomes the base for the search for Sita.
entries.kanda: Kishkindha Kanda; Sundara Kanda; Yuddha Kanda
entries.description: The narrative's alliance between Rama and Sugriva is formed in Kishkindha. From this region, Sugriva organizes the search parties that eventually identify Lanka as Sita's location.

shloka.sa:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं तस्मात्सप्तजनाश्रमात् ।
ददृशुस्तां दुराधर्षां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम् ॥
shloka.translation: After traveling far from the hermitage of the Seven Sages, they saw unconquerable Kishkindha, ruled by Vali.
shloka.edition: Numbering as shown on Ambuda; may differ from valmikiramayan.net and the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: Vanara realm where Rama allies with Sugriva and helps him regain the kingdom; it becomes the base for the search for Sita.

entries.name: Lanka
entries.role: Ravana's stronghold and the place where Sita is held; Rama's forces cross the sea and fight there.
entries.description: Lanka is the destination of Hanuman's reconnaissance and the final campaign to recover Sita. The epic depicts it as a fortified island city ruled by Ravana.

shloka.sa:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः |
त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह || ५-२-१
shloka.translation: Having crossed the impassable ocean, the mighty Hanuman saw Lanka situated on the summit of Trikuta, still in full strength.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Ravana's kingdom supplies the opposing force; Vibhishana separately defects to Rama.

entries.name: Panchavati
entries.modern_location: Panchavati area, Nashik, Maharashtra, India (traditional identification)
entries.role: Forest dwelling where Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana settle; Sita's abduction follows events there.
entries.description: The exiles establish a hermitage at Panchavati in the Dandaka forest. Encounters with Shurpanakha and the golden-deer deception lead to Sita's abduction.

shloka.sa:
इतो द्वि योजने तात बहु मूल फल उदकः |
देशो बहु मृगः श्रीमान् पंचवटि अभिविश्रुतः || ३-१३-१३
shloka.translation: Two yojanas from here lies the famed, splendid place called Panchavati, rich in roots, fruit, water, and deer.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Forest dwelling where Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana settle; Sita's abduction follows events there.

entries.name: Chitrakuta
entries.modern_location: Chitrakoot region on the Uttar Pradesh–Madhya Pradesh border, India
entries.ruler: No ruler named; Rama's forest retreat
entries.role: Early forest residence of Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana; Bharata visits Rama there to urge his return.
entries.description: Chitrakuta provides a peaceful refuge during the early part of the exile. Bharata's meeting with Rama there confirms Rama's resolve to honor the promised term away from Ayodhya.

shloka.sa: अथ दाशरथिः चित्रम् चित्र कूटम् अदर्शयत् | भार्याम् अमर सम्काशः शचीम् इव पुरम् दरः
shloka.translation: Then Dasharatha’s son, radiant as a god, showed his wife the wondrous Chitrakuta, as Purandara shows Shachi his city.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: Early forest residence of Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana; Bharata visits Rama there to urge his return.

entries.name: Dandakaranya
entries.modern_location: A broad traditional forest region across parts of central and eastern India; point shown near southern Chhattisgarh
entries.ruler: No single ruler identified; forest-dwelling sages and rakshasas appear in the region
entries.role: Extensive forest region traversed during the exile and the setting for many encounters with sages and rakshasas.
entries.description: Dandakaranya is a large narrative landscape rather than a single town. The exiles travel through its hermitage communities, while conflict with local rakshasas intensifies around Janasthana.

shloka.sa:
मानुषौ शस्त्र संपन्नौ चीर कृष्ण अजिन अंबरौ |
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् घोरम् प्रमदया सह || ३-१९-२२
shloka.translation: Two armed men, clad in bark and black deerskin, have entered the dreadful Dandaka forest with a woman.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: The forest's rakshasa forces, including Khara and Dushana at Janasthana, oppose Rama.

entries.name: Prayaga (Bharadvaja Ashrama)
entries.role: Bharadvaja's hermitage lies on the exiles' route from Ayodhya toward the forest and Chitrakuta.
entries.description: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana visit Bharadvaja and receive guidance about their onward journey. The episode links the departure from the settled kingdom with the deeper forest exile.

shloka.sa: प्रयागम् अभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूमम् उन्नतम् | अग्नेर् भगवतः केतुम् मन्ये सम्निहितः मुनिः || २-५४-५
shloka.translation: Look, Lakshmana, at the tall smoke near Prayaga, a sign of sacred fire; I think the sage is close by.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Bharadvaja's hermitage lies on the exiles' route from Ayodhya toward the forest and Chitrakuta.

entries.name: Shringaverapura (Nishada country)
entries.modern_location: Near the Ganges, northwest of Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, India (traditional identification)
entries.role: Guha welcomes Rama and helps the exiles cross the Ganges during their departure from Kosala.
entries.description: At Shringaverapura, Guha offers friendship and practical help to Rama's party. Their river crossing marks a further step away from Ayodhya and its political world.

shloka.sa: समुद्रमहीषीम् गङ्गाम् सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम् | आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरम् प्रति || २-५०-२६
shloka.translation: The mighty-armed Rama reached toward Shringaverapura, where Ganga, the ocean's queen, resounded with the calls of sarasa and krauncha birds.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Guha welcomes Rama and helps the exiles cross the Ganges during their departure from Kosala.

entries.name: Rameshwaram and the Setu
entries.modern_location: Rameswaram and the Palk Strait / Adam's Bridge region, Tamil Nadu–Sri Lanka
entries.ruler: Rama's campaign; Nala is credited with building the bridge
entries.role: Southern crossing point where Rama's army constructs a bridge over the sea toward Lanka.
entries.description: The bridge episode turns the search for Sita into a direct campaign against Ravana. Rameswaram is a modern traditional association with the mainland end of the crossing, not a precisely identified epic coordinate.

shloka.sa:
एष सेतुम् महाउत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः |
तम् अहम् धारयिष्यामि तथा हि एष यथा पिता || ६-२२-४५
shloka.translation: Let this greatly energetic monkey build a bridge across me; I shall support it, for he is like his father.
shloka.edition: Yuddha Kanda (book 6); the source page misprints the book number as 2, corrected here. Verse numbering may differ in other editions
shloka.note: The source page identifies Nala immediately before this verse.

entries.allegiance_role: Southern crossing point where Rama's army constructs a bridge over the sea toward Lanka.

entries.name: Pampa Lake
entries.modern_location: Near Anegundi and Hampi, Karnataka, India (traditional identification)
entries.ruler: No ruler named; visited by Rama and Lakshmana
entries.role: Lake and surrounding woodland in the Kishkindha region, where Rama encounters Shabari and continues toward Sugriva.
entries.description: Pampa is described as a beautiful waterside landscape during Rama's search for Sita. Its nearby hermitages and hills lead the brothers into the Kishkindha narrative.

shloka.sa:
ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते |
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः || ३-७२-१२
shloka.translation: The steadfast, heroic Sugriva dwells with four monkeys on excellent Mount Rishyamuka, made beautiful by the shores of Pampa.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Lake and surrounding woodland in the Kishkindha region, where Rama encounters Shabari and continues toward Sugriva.

entries.name: Rishyamukha Hill
entries.ruler: Sugriva and his companions take refuge there
entries.role: Hill refuge where Sugriva stays beyond Vali's reach and first meets Rama and Lakshmana.
entries.description: Rishyamukha is central to the meeting that creates the Rama–Sugriva alliance. Its protection is tied to Vali's inability to approach the mountain under a curse.

shloka.sa:
ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते |
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः || ३-७२-१२
shloka.translation: The steadfast, heroic Sugriva dwells with four monkeys on excellent Mount Rishyamuka, made beautiful by the shores of Pampa.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Hill refuge where Sugriva stays beyond Vali's reach and first meets Rama and Lakshmana.

entries.name: Kashi (Varanasi)
entries.ruler: A Kashi ruler is mentioned in the epic's royal genealogies; no single role in the main journey
entries.role: A northern kingdom named in the Ramayana's broader political and genealogical setting.
entries.kanda: Bala Kanda; other references vary by recension
entries.description: Kashi appears as part of the wider network of kingdoms surrounding the central story. It is not a major stop in Rama's forest journey, and later geographical identifications should not be treated as exact coordinates for the epic reference.

shloka.sa: रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्य पराक्रमः | राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानाम् इव वासवः
shloka.translation: Rama is dharma embodied, a good man of true valour, king of the whole world as Vasava is of the gods.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: A northern kingdom named in the Ramayana's broader political and genealogical setting.

entries.name: Kanyakubja (Kannauj)
entries.ruler: Kushika and his descendant Gadhi in the lineage tradition
entries.role: The ancestral kingdom associated with the story of Kushika, Gadhi, and Vishvamitra in the account of the sage's lineage.
entries.description: The Kanyakubja episode belongs to the background narrative about Vishvamitra's ancestry and transformation. Its location is conventionally connected with Kannauj, though that identification is historical-traditional rather than established by the epic itself.

shloka.sa: स पिता मम काकुत्स्थ गाधिः परमधार्मिकः | कुशवंशप्रसूतोऽस्मि कौशिको रघुनंदन
shloka.translation: That father of mine, O Kakutstha, was Gadhi, supremely righteous; I was born in the line of Kusha, and am called Kaushika, O delight of the Raghus.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: The ancestral kingdom associated with the story of Kushika, Gadhi, and Vishvamitra in the account of the sage's lineage.

entries.name: Mahendra Hill
entries.modern_location: Mahendragiri, Odisha, India (traditional identification; precise epic location uncertain)
entries.ruler: No ruler named; staging point for Hanuman's leap
entries.role: Mountain from which Hanuman launches his leap across the ocean toward Lanka.
entries.description: Mahendra marks the departure point for Hanuman's journey in search of Sita. The mountain's modern identification is not certain, and several regional traditions associate the name with different peaks.

shloka.sa: पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः | रीतीर्निर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः
shloka.translation: Pressed down by the mighty one, Mount Mahendra poured out streams of ore, gold, collyrium and silver.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: Mountain from which Hanuman launches his leap across the ocean toward Lanka.

entries.name: Janasthana
entries.modern_location: Traditionally associated with the Nashik region, Maharashtra, India
entries.role: Rakshasa-held territory in the Dandaka forest where Khara and his forces confront Rama.
entries.description: Janasthana is the base of Khara's power near Rama and Sita's forest dwelling. The battle there follows Sita's abduction and draws Ravana more directly into the conflict.

shloka.sa:
जानीषे त्वं जनस्थानं भ्राता यत्र खरो मम ।
दूषणश्च महाबाहुः स्वसा शूर्पणखा च मे ॥
shloka.translation: You know Janasthana, where my brother Khara lives, along with mighty Dushana and my sister Shurpanakha.
shloka.edition: Numbering as shown on Ambuda; may differ from valmikiramayan.net and the critical edition

entries.allegiance_role: Rakshasa-held territory in the Dandaka forest where Khara and his forces confront Rama.

entries.name: Matanga Ashrama
entries.modern_location: Traditionally placed near Pampa in the Hampi–Anegundi region, Karnataka, India
entries.ruler: Sage Matanga; Shabari dwells at the hermitage
entries.role: Hermitage associated with Shabari, whom Rama meets while searching for Sita.
entries.description: Shabari welcomes Rama at the hermitage and directs him onward toward the Pampa and Sugriva. The site's modern placement is a regional tradition rather than a securely established archaeological location.

shloka.sa:
पश्य मेघ घन प्रख्यम् मृग पक्षि समाकुलम् || ३-७४-२१
मतंग वनम् इति एव विश्रुतम् रघुनंदन |
shloka.translation: Behold, Raghunandana, the woodland crowded with animals and birds, resembling a mass of clouds, famed as Matanga Forest.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Hermitage associated with Shabari, whom Rama meets while searching for Sita.

entries.name: Agastya Ashrama
entries.modern_location: Dandaka forest region; exact site uncertain, with a representative point near Nashik, Maharashtra, India
entries.role: Hermitage visited by Rama, where Agastya offers counsel and arms before the party moves deeper into the forest.
entries.description: Agastya's hermitage is an important stop on Rama's forest route and a source of guidance. The text's broad forest geography does not establish a unique modern site for the ashrama.

shloka.sa:
स प्रविश्य आश्रम पदम् लक्ष्मणो राघव अनुजः |
अगस्त्य शिष्यम् आसाद्य वाक्यम् एतद् उवाच ह || ३-१२-१
shloka.translation: Entering the hermitage, Lakshmana, Raghava's younger brother, met Agastya's disciple and spoke these words.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Hermitage visited by Rama, where Agastya offers counsel and arms before the party moves deeper into the forest.

entries.name: Siddhashrama
entries.modern_location: Traditional site in the broader Mithila–Bihar region; exact modern location uncertain
entries.role: Forest hermitage where Rama and Lakshmana protect Vishvamitra's sacrifice from rakshasa attacks.
entries.description: Vishvamitra brings the princes to Siddhashrama during their early journey from Ayodhya. The episode gives Rama his first major combat role in the narrative.

shloka.sa: अयं सिद्धाश्रमो नाम प्रसादात्ते भविष्यति | सिद्धे कर्मणि देवेश उत्तिष्ठ भगवन्नितः || १-२९-१८
shloka.translation: By your grace, this place will be known as Siddhashrama. Now that the rite is complete, rise from here, lord of the gods.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Forest hermitage where Rama and Lakshmana protect Vishvamitra's sacrifice from rakshasa attacks.

entries.name: Sarayu River Bank
entries.modern_location: Sarayu River near Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, India
entries.ruler: Flows through the kingdom of Kosala
entries.role: River beside Ayodhya and an important geographical feature of the kingdom and the exiles' departure route.
entries.description: The Sarayu anchors the epic's opening description of Kosala and Ayodhya. Its banks also form part of the landscape the royal family leaves behind when Rama goes into exile.

shloka.sa: कोसलो नाम मुदितः स्फीतो जनपदो महान् | निविष्टः सरयूतीरे प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् || १-५-५
shloka.translation: There is a great kingdom named Kosala, joyful and prosperous, situated on the banks of the Sarayu and rich in wealth and grain.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: River beside Ayodhya and an important geographical feature of the kingdom and the exiles' departure route.

entries.name: Tamasa River Bank
entries.modern_location: Tamasa (Tons) River region near Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, India; precise crossing point uncertain
entries.ruler: No ruler named; first-night stopping place of Rama's party
entries.role: Riverside halt associated with Rama's first night away from Ayodhya during the exile.
entries.description: The Tamasa episode emphasizes the abrupt separation between Rama and the citizens who follow him from the capital. The exact modern river reach meant by the epic is uncertain.

shloka.sa: स तु तीरं समासाद्य तमसाया महामुनिः । शिष्यमाह स्थितं पार्श्वे दृष्ट्वा तीर्थमकर्दमम् ॥१-२-४॥
shloka.translation: Having reached the bank of the Tamasa and seen a clear, mud-free bathing place, the great sage spoke to his disciple standing beside him.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

entries.allegiance_role: Riverside halt associated with Rama's first night away from Ayodhya during the exile.

entries.name: Riksha allies (Jambavan)
entries.role: Jambavan and the riksha allies join Rama's campaign alongside Sugriva's vanaras.
entries.description: The epic describes Jambavan as a leader among the allied forest forces. Their exact territorial organization is not mapped as a separate kingdom in the text.

shloka.sa:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं तस्मात्सप्तजनाश्रमात् ।
ददृशुस्तां दुराधर्षां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम् ॥
shloka.translation: After traveling far from the hermitage of the Seven Sages, they saw unconquerable Kishkindha, ruled by Vali.

entries.name: Vibhishana
entries.role: Ravana's brother defects to Rama in Yuddha Kanda and is accepted as an ally.
entries.description: After rejecting Ravana's course, Vibhishana seeks refuge with Rama and later rules Lanka.

shloka.sa:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः |
त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह || ५-२-१
shloka.translation: Having crossed the impassable ocean, the mighty Hanuman saw Lanka situated on the summit of Trikuta, still in full strength.

stops.name: Ayodhya (Kosala)
stops.note: Rama sets out into exile with Sita and Lakshmana.

shloka.sa:
अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता |
 मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम् ||
shloka.translation: There was a city named Ayodhya, renowned throughout the world, which Manu, lord of humankind, had himself built.

stops.name: Shringaverapura (Nishada country)
stops.note: They cross the Ganga with the help of the Nishada chief Guha.

shloka.sa: समुद्रमहीषीम् गङ्गाम् सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम् | आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरम् प्रति || २-५०-२६
shloka.translation: The mighty-armed Rama reached toward Shringaverapura, where Ganga, the ocean's queen, resounded with the calls of sarasa and krauncha birds.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

stops.name: Prayaga (Bharadvaja Ashrama)
stops.note: They visit the sage Bharadvaja.

shloka.sa: प्रयागम् अभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूमम् उन्नतम् | अग्नेर् भगवतः केतुम् मन्ये सम्निहितः मुनिः || २-५४-५
shloka.translation: Look, Lakshmana, at the tall smoke near Prayaga, a sign of sacred fire; I think the sage is close by.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from critical edition)

stops.name: Chitrakuta
stops.note: They settle at Chitrakuta, where Bharata comes to beg Rama to return.

shloka.sa: अथ दाशरथिः चित्रम् चित्र कूटम् अदर्शयत् | भार्याम् अमर सम्काशः शचीम् इव पुरम् दरः
shloka.translation: Then Dasharatha’s son, radiant as a god, showed his wife the wondrous Chitrakuta, as Purandara shows Shachi his city.
shloka.edition: Numbering follows the page named in 'verified from' and may differ from the critical edition

stops.name: Dandakaranya
stops.note: They enter the Dandaka forest and its hermitages.

shloka.sa:
मानुषौ शस्त्र संपन्नौ चीर कृष्ण अजिन अंबरौ |
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् घोरम् प्रमदया सह || ३-१९-२२
shloka.translation: Two armed men, clad in bark and black deerskin, have entered the dreadful Dandaka forest with a woman.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

stops.name: Panchavati
stops.note: Their hut at Panchavati is where Surpanakha and later Ravana’s plot begin.

shloka.sa:
इतो द्वि योजने तात बहु मूल फल उदकः |
देशो बहु मृगः श्रीमान् पंचवटि अभिविश्रुतः || ३-१३-१३
shloka.translation: Two yojanas from here lies the famed, splendid place called Panchavati, rich in roots, fruit, water, and deer.
shloka.edition: Numbering as on valmikiramayan.net (Baroda/Gita Press-based; may differ from the critical edition)

stops.name: Janasthana
stops.note: Rama destroys the demon host of Khara and Dushana.

shloka.sa:
जानीषे त्वं जनस्थानं भ्राता यत्र खरो मम ।
दूषणश्च महाबाहुः स्वसा शूर्पणखा च मे ॥
shloka.translation: You know Janasthana, where my brother Khara lives, along with mighty Dushana and my sister Shurpanakha.
shloka.edition: Numbering as shown on Ambuda; may differ from valmikiramayan.net and the critical edition

stops.name: Rameshwaram and the Setu
stops.note: The vanara army builds the bridge to Lanka.

shloka.sa:
एष सेतुम् महाउत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः |
तम् अहम् धारयिष्यामि तथा हि एष यथा पिता || ६-२२-४५
shloka.translation: Let this greatly energetic monkey build a bridge across me; I shall support it, for he is like his father.
